title: Gypsy Without a Song and its lyricists
summary: Credits include Irving Gordon and Lou Singer; it came after Lost in Meditation.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Okay. How about "Gypsy Without a Song?"
Yeah, the same way. All those tunes started the same way. I would write it and if Duke liked it, he'd arrange it.
I didn't find Mills' name on that one anyplace. How did that one escape? That was while Duke was with Mills, right?
Yeah.
It was in 1938. The credits say Ellington, It says Tizol, Gordon and Singer. That was Lou Singer -- would that be Irving Gordon?
No, no. Lou Singer I think ...
But it's got four names; it's got Gordon there, too. Would that be Irving Gordon or some other Gordon?
That was the husband friend of the girl who used to go with Red Stewart -- what was her name?
Claire Gordon?
Claire Gordon, yeah.
Her husband, Irving?
Irving Gordon, yeah.
So he and Lou Singer wrote the lyrics to "Gypsy Without a Song?"
I hate to say yes or no -- but if they put it in there, Lou Singer did do a couple of things for me on my songs, so it must be true.
What can you tell me about "Gypsy Without a Song," about when you wrote it, how you wrote it, or ...
"Gypsy Without a Song" was after "Lost in Meditation," I think.
That's a beautiful tune, "Gypsy Without A Song."
Oh, that was her favorite one.
Did the title come from the lyrics? Did you have anything to do with the title of that one?
No.
